headline: Rector at Graz University of Technology
summary:
Horst Bischof received his M.S. and Ph.D. degree in computer science from the Vienna University of Technology in 1990 and 1993. In 1998 he got his Habilitation (venia docendi) for applied computer science. Currently he is Vice Rector for Research at Graz University of Technology and Professor at the Institute for Computer Graphics and Vision at the Graz University of Technology, Austria. H. Bischof is a member of the scientific board of Joanneum Research.  His research interests include object recognition, visual learning, on-line and life-long learning, motion and tracking, visual surveillance and biometrics and medical computer vision where he has published more than 750 peer reviewed scientific papers.

Horst Bischof was General Chair of CVPR 2015 and ECCV2018. He was program co-chair of ECCV2006 and ECCV 2020. He is multiple times Area chair of all major vision conferences. He was Associate Editor for IEEE Trans. on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, Pattern Recognition, Computer and Informatics and the Journal of Universal Computer Science.

Horst Bischof is member of the European academy of sciences and has received several awards  >20 among them the Most Influential Paper over the Decade Award from MVA 2019, the Jan Konderink award at ECCV 2018 and the 29th Pattern Recognition award in 2002, the main price of the German Association for Pattern Recognition DAGM in 2007 and 2012, the Best scientific paper award at the BMCV 2007, the BMVC best demo award 2012 and the Best scientific paper awards at the ICPR 2008, ICPR2010, PCV 2010, AAPR2010 and ACCV 2012.

Development of translational 3D in vitro models for breast cancer research.

The tissue microenvironment is crucial for many pathological processes such as breast cancer. Overcoming limitations of conventional 2D cell culture techniques, our approach using a semi-synthetic biomaterial to reconstruct the matrix in our 3D cultures reflect closer cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions involved in breast cancer in situ.

Dr. Koch is a Full Professor in the Department of Biomedical Sciences, Ontario Veterinary College, University of Guelph, Canada. He received his Veterinary degree from the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University, Copenhagen, Denmark. Dr. Koch’s current research focus is on stem cell and tissue engineering-based therapies with joint cartilage repair being the main area of investigation. Studies on equine and canine stem cells, joint cartilage and synovial joint health are pursued in parallel. Within this applied research approach basic mechanistic insights of joint homeostasis and the chondrogenic cell fate is sought including studies in the area of cell mechanobiology. Emerging research areas of interest include tendon and ligament repair and the regulatory roles of microRNA. Novel therapies applied in horses and dogs with natural spontaneous disease serve as important translational pre-clinical animal models of similar human diseases.

His work has resulted in one spin-off company, eQcell Inc, which is developing stem cell services for horses and dogs. He serves as Chief Executive Officer and Chief Scientific Officer.

headline: Professor of Robotics and Perception at the University of Zurich
summary: Davide Scaramuzza is a Professor of Robotics and Perception at the University of Zurich. He did his Ph.D. at ETH Zurich, a postdoc at the University of Pennsylvania, and was a visiting professor at Stanford University. His research focuses on autonomous, agile navigation of mini drones using standard and event-based cameras. He pioneered autonomous, vision-based navigation of drones, which inspired the navigation algorithm of the NASA Mars helicopter and many drone companies. In 2022, his team demonstrated that an AI-powered drone could outperform the world champion of drone racing, a result published in Nature. He has been consulting the United Nations on disaster response, the Fukushima Action Plan, disarmament, and AI for good. For his research contributions, he has won many awards, including the very recent IEEE Kiyo Tomiyasu Technical Field Award, the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society Early Career Award, a European Research Council Consolidator Grant, and many paper awards, including the IROS 2023 Best Paper Award, the IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters' and Transactions on Robotics best paper awards, and a 2023 CVPR Best Paper Award finalist. Davide contributed significantly to visual-inertial state estimation, vision-based agile navigation of microdrones, and low-latency, robust perception with event cameras. His results have been transferred to many products, from drones to automobiles, cameras, AR/VR headsets, and mobile devices. Davide counts several entrepreneurial achievements: in 2015, he co-founded Zurich-Eye, which became Meta Zurich, which developed the world-leading virtual-reality headset Meta Quest. In 2020, he co-founded SUIND, which builds autonomous drones for precision agriculture. Many aspects of his research have been featured in the media, such as The New York Times, The Economist, and Forbes.

headline: Rector at Graz University of Technology
summary:
Horst Bischof received his M.S. and Ph.D. degree in computer science from the Vienna University of Technology in 1990 and 1993. In 1998 he got his Habilitation (venia docendi) for applied computer science. Currently he is Vice Rector for Research at Graz University of Technology and Professor at the Institute for Computer Graphics and Vision at the Graz University of Technology, Austria. H. Bischof is a member of the scientific board of Joanneum Research.  His research interests include object recognition, visual learning, on-line and life-long learning, motion and tracking, visual surveillance and biometrics and medical computer vision where he has published more than 750 peer reviewed scientific papers.

Horst Bischof was General Chair of CVPR 2015 and ECCV2018. He was program co-chair of ECCV2006 and ECCV 2020. He is multiple times Area chair of all major vision conferences. He was Associate Editor for IEEE Trans. on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, Pattern Recognition, Computer and Informatics and the Journal of Universal Computer Science.

Horst Bischof is member of the European academy of sciences and has received several awards  >20 among them the Most Influential Paper over the Decade Award from MVA 2019, the Jan Konderink award at ECCV 2018 and the 29th Pattern Recognition award in 2002, the main price of the German Association for Pattern Recognition DAGM in 2007 and 2012, the Best scientific paper award at the BMCV 2007, the BMVC best demo award 2012 and the Best scientific paper awards at the ICPR 2008, ICPR2010, PCV 2010, AAPR2010 and ACCV 2012.

Development of translational 3D in vitro models for breast cancer research.

headline: Founder, Chief Executive Officer & Chief Scientific Officer at eQcell Inc.
summary:
Dr. Koch is a Full Professor in the Department of Biomedical Sciences, Ontario Veterinary College, University of Guelph, Canada. He received his Veterinary degree from the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University, Copenhagen, Denmark. Dr. Koch’s current research focus is on stem cell and tissue engineering-based therapies with joint cartilage repair being the main area of investigation. Studies on equine and canine stem cells, joint cartilage and synovial joint health are pursued in parallel. Within this applied research approach basic mechanistic insights of joint homeostasis and the chondrogenic cell fate is sought including studies in the area of cell mechanobiology. Emerging research areas of interest include tendon and ligament repair and the regulatory roles of microRNA. Novel therapies applied in horses and dogs with natural spontaneous disease serve as important translational pre-clinical animal models of similar human diseases.

His work has resulted in one spin-off company, eQcell Inc, which is developing stem cell services for horses and dogs. He serves as Chief Executive Officer and Chief Scientific Officer.

Supplemental to his research program he participates as a senior clinician in the out-of-hours emergency service at the Veterinary Teaching Hospital at the Ontario Veterinary College for the  Large Animal Internal Medicine Section.

headline: Professor of Robotics and Perception at the University of Zurich
summary: Davide Scaramuzza is a Professor of Robotics and Perception at the University of Zurich. He did his Ph.D. at ETH Zurich, a postdoc at the University of Pennsylvania, and was a visiting professor at Stanford University. His research focuses on autonomous, agile navigation of mini drones using standard and event-based cameras. He pioneered autonomous, vision-based navigation of drones, which inspired the navigation algorithm of the NASA Mars helicopter and many drone companies. In 2022, his team demonstrated that an AI-powered drone could outperform the world champion of drone racing, a result published in Nature. He has been consulting the United Nations on disaster response, the Fukushima Action Plan, disarmament, and AI for good. For his research contributions, he has won many awards, including the very recent IEEE Kiyo Tomiyasu Technical Field Award, the IEEE Robotics and Automation Society Early Career Award, a European Research Council Consolidator Grant, and many paper awards, including the IROS 2023 Best Paper Award, the IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters' and Transactions on Robotics best paper awards, and a 2023 CVPR Best Paper Award finalist. Davide contributed significantly to visual-inertial state estimation, vision-based agile navigation of microdrones, and low-latency, robust perception with event cameras. His results have been transferred to many products, from drones to automobiles, cameras, AR/VR headsets, and mobile devices. Davide counts several entrepreneurial achievements: in 2015, he co-founded Zurich-Eye, which became Meta Zurich, which developed the world-leading virtual-reality headset Meta Quest. In 2020, he co-founded SUIND, which builds autonomous drones for precision agriculture. Many aspects of his research have been featured in the media, such as The New York Times, The Economist, and Forbes.

headline: Director, AI Initiative, KAUST; Scientific Director, Swiss AI Lab, IDSIA; Adj. Prof. of AI, Univ. Lugano; Co-Founder & Chief Scientist, NNAISENSE
summary: The New York Times headlined: "When A.I. Matures, It May Call Jürgen Schmidhuber 'Dad'." Since age 15, his main goal has been to build a self-improving A.I. smarter than himself, then retire. His lab's deep learning artificial neural networks based on ideas published in the "Annus Mirabilis" 1990-1991 have revolutionised machine learning and A.I. By 2017, they were on over 3 billion smartphones, and used billions of times per day, for Facebook’s automatic translation, Google’s speech recognition, Google Translate, Apple’s Siri & QuickType, Amazon’s Alexa, etc. Generative AI is also based on his work: he introduced artificial curiosity & generative adversarial networks (1990, now widely used), self-supervised pre-training for deep learning (1991, the "P" in "ChatGPT" stands for "pre-trained"), unnormalised linear Transformers (1991, the "T" in "ChatGPT" stands for "Transformer"), and meta-learning machines that learn to learn (since 1987, now widely used). His lab also produced LSTM, the most cited AI of the 20th century, and the LSTM-inspired Highway Net, the first very deep feedforward net with hundreds of layers (ResNet, the most cited AI of the 21st century, is an open-gated Highway Net). In 2006-2010, he published the "formal theory of fun and creativity." Elon Musk tweeted: "Schmidhuber invented everything." He is recipient of numerous awards, Co-Chair of the KAUST Gen AI Center in KSA, Scientific Director of the Swiss AI Lab IDSIA, and co-founder & former President of NNAISENSE. He is a frequent keynote speaker at major events, and advising various governments on A.I. strategies. More: https://people.idsia.ch/~juergen/blog.html

honors.description:
EY Schweiz hat im Jahr 2021 zum 24. Mal herausragende Schweizer Unternehmer ausgezeichnet. Der EY Entrepreneur Of The Year wurde am 29. Oktober vor 250 geladenen Gästen in Zürich verliehen. Es wurden fünf Gewinner in vier Kategorien ausgezeichnet.

Stefan Muff, Gründer der Luzerner Firma Axon Active, ist in der Kategorie Dienstleistung & Handel zum Sieger gekürt worden. Seine Firma entwickelt und testet Software mit Fokus auf die digitale Transformation. Muff ist auch der Gründer des Geodatenanbieters Endoxon, den er 2006 verkauft hat, und der heute als Google Maps bekannt ist. Die Jury ehrt ihn, weil er ein „Visionär und Gestalter eines Ökosystems der IT-Branche ist, wie man es hierzulande nur selten antrifft“.

Quelle: Luzern-business.ch & Luzerner Zeitung

headline: Unternehmer, Visionär & Investor
summary:
Alles begann in den Achtzigerjahren mit meinem "Traumjob" beim Bundesamt für Raumplanung. Eines Tages erhielt ich den Auftrag, ein räumliches Informationssystem aufzubauen, und aus diesem Antrieb heraus wagte ich den Schritt in die Selbstständigkeit. Gemeinsam mit meinem Bruder Bruno gründete ich im Jahr 1988 die Symplan Map AG, die später zur Endoxon AG in Luzern wurde.

Unsere Geodatentechnologie, basierend auf Luftbildkarten, weckte das Interesse großer amerikanischer IT-Konzerne. Im Jahr 2006 verkauften wir schließlich Endoxon an Google. Was viele Google-Nutzer nicht wissen: Diese Kartentechnologie trug später zur Entwicklung von Google Maps bei.

Im Jahr 2008 legten wir dann den Grundstein für die heutige Axon-Gruppe, deren Hauptsitz sich im malerischen Luzerner Schlössli Schönegg befindet.

Seither setzen wir uns Tag für Tag intensiv mit den Herausforderungen der digitalen Transformation auseinander und streben nach Disruption und Agilität. Es ist unsere Mission, mit unvergleichlicher Kompetenz und einer starken visionären Leidenschaft wegweisende Lösungen zu gestalten, die unseren Kunden eine erfolgreiche digitale Transformation ermöglichen.

Die Anfänge meines Unternehmens waren geprägt von der Faszination für die neuesten Technologien. Seitdem haben wir uns kontinuierlich weiterentwickelt und arbeiten unermüdlich daran, die Zukunft der digitalen Transformation aktiv mitzugestalten. Unsere Expertise und unser Engagement spiegeln sich in den zukunftsweisenden Lösungen wider, die wir entwickeln und implementieren, um den sich ständig wandelnden Anforderungen unserer Kunden gerecht zu werden.

headline: Founder & Director Pflege PBS, Professor in Nursing Diagnostics & former ACENDIO President
summary:
Maria Müller-Staub was Professor Adjunct in Nursing Diagnostics at Hanze University, Nursing Department, in Groningen (NL). Formerly, she was Full Professor  in Acute Care at the Institute for Nursing Science, ZHAW University, Winterthur and Program Director of nursing research and research transfer courses.
She is an excellent nurse educator at graduate levels in nursing and supervisor of doctoral students. As an expert in curriculum development, she was Dean of a nursing school offering advanced nursing programs. 

Maria Müller-Staub is Founder & Director of Pflege PBS (Nurse Consulting, Teaching, & Research), Wil, Switzerland (CH). She implements nursing language related to the classifications of nursing diagnoses, interventions and outcomes (NANDA-I, NIC & NOC) in Swiss and German hospitals and nursing education programs. 

Her main focus in research and education is evidence-based practice based on nursing diagnostics, clinical decision making and critical thinking. She leads research and practice projects on standards for nursing documentation, nursing care quality and Clinical Information Systems (CIS). 

The instrument Quality of Diagnoses, Interventions and Outcomes (Q-DIO) was developed and tested to measure the quality of the nursing process as an audit tool. The Q-DIO was translated and tested in the languages German, English, Brazilian, Portugese, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Slovenian, French and Bahasa Indonesian. 

Maria Müller-Staub has 356 publications and presented more than 200 oral papers. She was a lecturer in national and international nursing programs.

See further CV information and list of publications at:
https://www.pflege-pbs.ch

headline: CEO at Speratum Biopharma
summary:
I previously worked as a Post-Doctoral Associate in the Department of Surgery at Baylor College of Medicine (BCM), in the laboratories of Dr. Qizhi Yao and Dr. Changyi Chen, with a focus on developing RNAi-based therapeutics for the treatment of cancer. 

That work is the basis for Speratum, a pre-clinical stage cancer therapy company with exclusive licenses for multiple technologies originally developed at BCM.  At Speratum we combine RNA interference (RNAi) and synthetic biology with a novel, polymeric nanoparticle-based delivery system. Our main focus is  on the treatment of pancreatic and ovarian cancers. We are currently developing novel targeted antiviral applications of our technology. 

I have been executive director of Speratum since its foundation in 2014. I have Ph.D. in Molecular Virology and Microbiology from BCM, an MS in Entrepreneurial Biotechnology from the Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Program (STEP) at Case, and a BS in molecular biology from Florida Tech. 

I have previously worked as a consultant to biotechnology start-up companies and governmental organizations. My work has contributed to the development of projects ranging from medical devices to HIV research. 

I am a founding member of the Scientific Ethics Committee for the Ministry of Health of Costa Rica, founding member of CRBiomed, the biomedical cluster of Costa Rica, and am a member of the Aspen Global Leadership Network (AGLN), the Aspen Institute, and the Central American Leadership Initiative (CALI).

I've had the chance to learn from top physicians and scientists during my training at University of Munich and Yale University, and to learn from the finest editors at the German School of Journalism and at different media outlets, e.g. German daily "Süddeutsche Zeitung", German public radio "Bayerischer Rundfunk" and German news magazine "Der Spiegel".

After my training I worked in the Department of Anaesthesiology at University of Munich's hospital and at SPIEGEL ONLINE, "Der Spiegel"'s digital news outlet, before moving on to "Wort & Bild Verlag", where I am currently the Executive Editor.

I am always happy to connect with people, especially those interested in the same topics as me. Please feel free to contact me.

headline: Evolutionary Neuroscience of Language
summary: Martin Meyer and his group are interested in all aspects of the relationship between brain and language. We ask how (spoken) language is used to understand the brain, and how the brain is used to understand (spoken) language. Using the full arsenal of modern neuroimaging approaches, we have investigated how right and left hemispheres contribute to decoding and understanding spoken utterances. In particular, we are interested in the influences of different forms of hearing loss and brain atrophy on the neuroplasticity of speech comprehension in different languages. Currently, we are working on a model of the evolutionary properties and origins of prosody and speech rhythm and their links to neural circuits of the motor system and aim to fathom the neural underpinning of structure planning during language production. Another area of our research examines the basis and treatment options for central hearing disorders, particularly chronic subjective tinnitus and its limiting effect on speech understanding and everyday communication.

headline: Director of the TUM Institute for Ethics in Artificial Intelligence bei Technische Universität München
summary:
Christoph Lütge studied business informatics and philosophy in Braunschweig, Paris, Göttingen and Berlin. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Pittsburgh (1997) and research fellow at the University of California, San Diego (1998). After taking his PhD in philosophy in 1999, Lütge held a position as assistant professor at the Chair for Philosophy and Economics of the University of Munich (LMU) from 1999 to 2007, where he also took his habilitation in 2005. He was acting professor at Witten/Herdecke University (2007-2008) and at Braunschweig University of Technology (2008-2010). Since 2010, he holds the Peter Löscher Chair in Business Ethics at the Technical University of Munich. In 2019, Lütge was appointed director of the new TUM Institute for Ethics in Artificial Intelligence. He has held visiting positions in Venice (2003), Kyoto (2015), Taipei (2015), at Harvard (2019) and the University of Stockholm (2020). In 2020, he was appointed Distinguished Visiting Professor of the University of Tokyo. His main areas of interest are ethics of AI, ethics of digitization, business ethics, foundations of ethics as well as philosophy of the social sciences and economics. His major publications include "Business Ethics: An Economically Informed Perspective" (Oxford University Press, 2021, with Matthias Uhl), "An Introduction to Ethics in Robotics and AI“ (Springer, 2021, with coauthors) and "The Ethics of Competition” (Elgar, 2019; Japanese edition with Keio University Press, 2020).
He has been a member of the Ethics Commission on Automated and Connected Driving of the German Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure (2016-17), as well as of the European AI Ethics initiative AI4People (2018-). He has also done consulting work for the Singapore Economic Development Board and the Canadian Transport Commission.

Digitale Netzwerke statt Silodenken: Teilen und Weiterentwickeln von Wissen bedeuten Schubkraft für Innovation und dringend nötiger Veränderung
Cloud Computing hat Informationstechnologie wie Strom aus der Steckdose verfügbar gemacht: klein und schnell überholt groß und träge jederzeit.

- verteilte Strukturen statt zentrale Datenhaltung
- Digitaler Besitz lässt uns die Kontrolle über unsere Daten zurückgewinnen
- Das Metaverse erschließt uns neue Welten
- Composable Systems basierend auf Open Source wird Kreativität explodieren lassen
- Dezentrale autonome Organisationen lassen uns Zusammenarbeit neu denken

Die Herausforderungen unserer Zeit sind groß. Die Chancen sind es auch.

summary:
2009 - Martin is department head at Fraunhofer IESE. 
He is heading the Embedded Systems Engineering department. 
Core competencies of the department include: 
- Model-based Systems Engineering, esp. RE and System Architecting/Design.
- Variation Management =  Variant & LifeCycle Management 

His specialties: 
• Software and Systems Product Line Engineering, esp. architectures and implementation
• CPS-Architectures with focus on self-adaptivity, runtime adaptation and context-awareness
• Model-Based Systems Engineering

More on his C.V.:
Martin received his diploma in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering in 1997 from the University of Kaiserslautern. Between 1998 and 2003, he worked in a special research project on large system development with generic methods (SFB 501), where he developed several approaches for architecting and managing software product families.

In 2004, he received his Ph.D. (Dr. Ing.) in Computer Science in the field of variability management from the University of Kaiserslautern and got affiliated with the Product Line Architecture department of the Fraunhofer Institute for Empirical Software Engineering (IESE) in Kaiserslautern.  As a project manager, he conducted several applied research and technology transfer projects in the area of software product lines, component-based development, configuration support, and adaptive systems. From 2006-2009 he has coordiniated Fraunhofer IESE’s competence center on Ambient Intelligence (AMI) and Ambient Assisted Living (AAL). His special interest in AMI/AAL were reference architectures with focus on interoperability, adaptability and trustworthiness and context management.

occupation: PwC | Artificial Intelligence Partner | Transformation – Technology – Trust | Startup Investor and Advisor
headline: PwC | Artificial Intelligence Partner | Transformation – Technology – Trust | Startup Investor and Advisor
summary:
Veränderungen sind nicht immer leicht, aber in unserem Digitalzeitalter nötig, um zu bestehen und zu wachsen. Ich unterstütze Unternehmen bei ihren Transformationsprozessen, helfe ihnen, Probleme und Herausforderungen zu erkennen und langfristige Lösungen zu implementieren. 

Bei PwC bin ich als Partner spezialisiert auf #AI und unterstütze Kunden, die Technologie verantwortungsvoll einsetzen zu können. Change ist mein Antrieb. Um Künstliche Intelligenz erfolgreich im Betrieb zu operationalisieren, braucht es neben der Transformation und Technologie auch Vertrauen als essentielle Zutat. Meine tiefe Überzeugung ist, dass Trust Kern erfolgreicher Geschäftsmodelle ist. 
In über zwanzig Jahren Berufserfahrung habe auch ich einige Veränderungen durchlaufen - von Cyber, über Cloud zu AI und vom (Co-)Gründer über verschiedene Consulting Stationen zu PwC. 

Diesen Erfahrungsschatz nutze ich, um meine Kunden strategisch und mit Weitblick durch ihre individuelle Transformation zu navigieren. Um die besten Lösungen für unsere Kund*innen und die Gesellschaft zu finden, bewegen wir uns immer vor der Welle - mit dem Ziel, erfolgreiche Lösungen für eine neue digitale Zukunft zu gestalten.

headline: Artificial Intelligence | Innovation | Ecosystems
summary:
There are three major themes in my career: Innovation, Digital Technologies and Ecosystems. 
I am fascinated by the innovative possibilities of digital technologies, and how they can be implemented quickly and successfully through Ecosystems. 

For the past 10 plus years, I’ve been particularly involved with the topic of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning , how it gives rise to innovative solutions and the strategic importance of collaboration, strategic partnerships and ecosystems .

Current activities
With the AI.FUND (https://ai-fund.vc/) we invest in European AI startups.
I am the Managing Director of KI-Allianz Baden-Württemberg eG (https://ki-allianz.de/), which aims to establish a centre and ecosystem for AI in the state that is competitive and visible throughout Europe and internationally.
With ADI Innovation (https://www.adi.de/) and IBHO Management (https://ibho.de/) , I advise enterprises, startups and the public sector on the implementation of digital transformation and applications of AI.

In 2020 I have been nominated by the German government as an Member of the Global Partnership on AI (https://gpai.ai/), where I advance the topics of innovation & commercialization of AI with experts from 20 countries.
Since 2020 I support the German Federal Agency for disruptive Innovations (https://www.sprind.org/en/) as an expert for AI
Since 2018 I support the German Government in the development of the German AI Strategy.

Past activities:

Through AI.Hamburg I promoted the transfer and use of AI in companies in Hamburg and Northern Germany. Together with other AI initiatives, we founded AI4Germany to foster collaboration and bring Germany into the AI age.
At appliedAI / UnternehmerTUM, I expanded the AI Ecosystem in Germany and Europe.
I supported the Tübingen AI Competence Center and the Cyber Valley Initiative as General Manager with a focus on the transfer of AI from science into business.
At IBM, I helped to roll out the topic of AI and Watson Health in Europe.
For almost 20 years, I held various management positions at SAP. I introduced new technologies to the market (ERP R/3), built up the global partnership with Microsoft, helped initiate the global technology partner program, was responsible for the product portfolio in the public sector and built up strategic risk management (today Foresight) for the Executive Board.

honors.title: Fellow of the European Association of Artificial Intelligence (EurAI)
honors.description:
The EurAI Fellows programme recognises European AI researchers who have made exceptional contributions to the field. A call for nominations is issued to Fellows and EurAI member societies annually.

The EurAI Fellows program has been started in 1999 to recognize individuals who have made significant, sustained contributions to the field of artificial intelligence (AI) in Europe. Fellows' accomplishments range from pioneering advances in the theory of AI, to unusual accomplishments in AI technology and applications. Usually only individuals who have made contributions to AI for a decade or more after receiving their Ph.D. (or are at an equivalent career stage) will be selected. Leadership in EurAI or EurAI member societies, support of forums for the exchange of ideas, and extended service for the international AI community also play a role in the selection process. Evidence of technical contribution will often be in the form of publications, but other evidence will also be considered, such as patent awards or statements of longstanding contribution to an industrial group effort. The EurAI Fellows Program honors only a very small percentage of the total membership of all EurAI member societies (up to a maximum of 3%).

headline: German AI Award, AAAI/EurAI/ELLIS/AAIA Fellow, Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz, Professor for AI & Machine Learning at TU Darmstadt, Founding Co-Director Hessian.AI, DFKI, CAIRNE, ELLIS
summary:
I am a Full Professor for Machine Learning (ML) at the CS Department of the TU Darmstadt University, Germany. I am heading the machine learning lab and I am also with the Centre for Cognitive Science. After receiving my Ph.D. from the University of Freiburg in 2006, I was with the MIT, Fraunhofer IAIS, the University of Bonn, and the TU Dortmund. My main research interests are statistical relational artificial intelligence (AI), probabilistic programming, and deep probabilistic learning. Overall, I  have published over 180 peer-reviewed technical papers.

I am a Fellow of the European Association for Artificial Intelligence (EurAI), a Fellow of the European Laborator for Learning and Intelligent Systems (ELLIS), and a key supporter of the Confederation of Laboratories for Artificial Intelligence in Europe (CLAIRE). I was named a Top 100 Influential Scholar 2018 for Artificial Intelligence by AMiner and received the BILANZ German AI Award (Deutscher KI-Preis) 2019, accompanied by a prize of EURO100.000, as well as several best paper (TPM 2019, AIIDE 2015, ECML 2006), outstanding reviewer awards (ECCV 2016, AAAI 2013), a Fraunhofer Attract research grant with a budget of 2.5 Million Euro over 5 years (2008-2013), and the EurAI (formerly ECCAI) AI Dissertation Award 2006 for the best Ph.D. thesis in the field of Artificial Intelligence in Europe. I regularly serves on the PC (often at senior level) for several top conference (AAAI, ICML, IJCAI, NeurIPS, UAI, WWW, ICLR, KDD, CVPR and others), am an elected PC co-chair of ECML PKDD 2020, was the General Co-Chair of UAI 2018, and co-chaired the scientific program committees (PC) of UAI 2017 as well as ECML PKDD 2013. I am the founding Speciality Editor-in-Chief for Machine Learning and AI of Frontiers in Big Data, and (past) action editor of IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence (TPAMI), Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research (JAIR), Artificial Intelligence Journal (AIJ), Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery (DAMI), and Machine Learning Journal (MLJ).

headline: Tech Entrepreneur | Currently building and scaling our portfolio of 5 XR and AI companies🚀 | ⬇️ Learn more ⬇️
summary:
Als ich 14 Jahre alt geworden bin, wurde mir zum ersten Mal schlagartig eines bewusst: 

Viele Menschen leben unter ihrem Potenzial und könnten so viel mehr aus ihrem einzigen Leben machen. Das finde ich sehr traurig und das Schlimmste für mich daran ist, dass die Gründe dafür meistens unbegründete Ängste oder gesellschaftliche Normen sind.
 
Diese Erkenntnis und der damit verbundene Schlüsselmoment in meinem Leben hat mich offen gesprochen nachhaltig geprägt. Ich habe mir daraufhin fest zum Ziel gemacht, nichts im Leben jemals zu bereuen, alles aus dem einen Leben zu machen, was ich mir erträume und anderen zu helfen, das Gleiche tun zu können. 
 
In der Uni versuchten mir Dozenten zu erklären, dass ich einen klassischen Weg gehen müsse, um erfolgreich zu werden. Ich habe die Uni nach einem halben Semester geschmissen und gründete mein erstes Unternehmen mit meinem damals ganzen Ersparten (3.000€). Vielleicht auch, um der Welt zu beweisen, dass es vielleicht doch anders geht, als es im Lehrbuch steht. 

Auch wenn eine erfolgreiche Firma aufzubauen, dann doch nicht so einfach war, wie im jugendlichen Leichtsinn gedacht, durfte ich schnell dazu lernen und war mit 21 Jahren bereits Gastdozent in meiner damaligen Uni. Um darüber zu sprechen, wie man als junger Mensch erfolgreich wird. Das hat mir erstmal eine gute Portion Selbstbewusstsein gegeben :-P
 
Aus dem kleinen Unternehmen wurde ein größeres Unternehmen und darauf folgten 5 Weitere. Wir wurden zu einer Unternehmensgruppe, die mittlerweile über 350 Technologie bezogene Projekte für Fortune 500/100 und den Mittelstand umgesetzt hat und aus über 80 Mitarbeitern besteht. 
Doch warum erzähle ich das? 
 
Ich möchte eine Welt, in der jeder Mensch sein volles Potenzial ausleben kann und damit sein eigenes Leben und das seiner Mitmenschen bereichert.  Ich möchte, dass Menschen sehen, dass man mit 3.000 Euro und ohne Investor gründen kann und einige Jahre später, mit einem Alter von 27 Jahren, daraus achtstellige Unternehmensbewertungen (10M+) resultieren können. 
Wenn man an sich glaubt und bereit ist, die notwendige Energie zu investieren.
 
Ob man Unternehmer/in oder etwas anderes werden will, ist mir dabei ziemlich egal. 
Ich möchte einfach Menschen davor bewahren, mit 70 zu realisieren, dass man sein Leben und sein Potenzial aufgrund von schwachsinnigen gesellschaftlichen Normen nicht ausgelebt hat. 

Unser Ziel ist es nun auch über Social Media unsere Reise zu teilen, um euch damit Mut zu machen, die eigene Lebensvision umzusetzen oder sie zu finden.

Earned after obtaining a research doctorate, such as a PhD, habilitation requires that the candidate write a professorial thesis (or habilitation thesis) based on independent scholarship, reviewed by and defended before an academic committee in a process similar to that of the doctoral dissertation. headline: Professor in Computer Engineering and Member of the Board of Directors at LRZ
summary:
Martin Schulz is a Full Professor and Chair for Computer Architecture and Parallel Systems at the Technische Universität München (TUM), which he joined in 2017, as well as a member of the board of directors at the Leibniz Supercomputing Centre. Prior to that, he held positions at the Center for Applied Scientific Computing (CASC) at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) and Cornell University. He earned his Doctorate in Computer Science in 2001 from TUM and a Master of Science in Computer Science from UIUC.

Martin's research interests include parallel and distributed architectures and applications; performance monitoring, modeling and analysis; memory system optimization; parallel programming paradigms; tool support for parallel programming; power-aware parallel computing; and fault tolerance at the application and system level, as well as quantum computing and quantum computing architectures and programming, with a special focus on HPC and QC integration.

Martin has published over 250 peer-reviewed papers and currently serves as the chair of the MPI Forum, the standardization body for the Message Passing Interface, one of the dominating standard in High-Performance Computing. He was a recipient of the IEEE/ACM Gordon Bell Award in 2006 and an R&D 100 award in 2011. He served on many conference and workshop organizing and program committees, including as program chair for ISC 2021, PC area chair at IPDPS 2021 and general chair of EuroMPI 2021.

headline: Verband der leitenden Krankenhausärzte e.V. (VLK
summary:
Der Verband leitender Krankenhausärztinnen und -ärzte e.V. (VLK) ist die einzige ärztliche Interessenvertretung in Deutschland, die sich sowohl bundesweit als auch auf Ebene der 16 Landesverbände für die vielfältigen Anliegen der leitenden Krankenhausärztinnen und -ärzte einsetzt. Er vertritt diese zielgerichtet gegenüber Klinikträgern, Versicherungsträgern, Politik und Öffentlichkeit. 

Der VLK bietet seinen Mitgliedern eine Reihe von Leistungen, die darauf abzielen, ihre Zukunftsfähigkeit zu stärken:

Vertrags- und Rechtsberatung: Qualifizierte rechtliche Beratung im Zusammenhang mit Dienstverträgen sowie fundierte Beratung in allen beruflichen Angelegenheiten vor gerichtlichen Auseinandersetzungen. Die Rechtsberatung ist im Mitgliedsbeitrag enthalten; eine darüber hinausgehende Rechtsvertretung ist kostenpflichtig. 

Organisationsberatung: Unterstützung bei der Umsetzung krankenhausspezifischer Prozesse mit dem Ziel positiv umsetzbarer Veränderungen sowie Coaching bei Personal- und Prozessveränderungen. Der Erstkontakt ist im Mitgliedsbeitrag enthalten; Konzept und Umsetzung werden nach Aufwand berechnet. 

Berufsbegleitung und Weiterbildung: Beratung und Begleitung in Ermächtigungs- und Befugnisfragen zur Weiterbildung, bei der beruflichen Entwicklung und Karriereplanung sowie Unterstützung auf dem Weg zur leitenden Ärztin oder zum leitenden Arzt. Diese Beratung ist im Mitgliedsbeitrag enthalten. 

Personalvermittlung: Vermittlung von qualifiziertem ärztlichem Personal in allen Funktionsebenen. Die Vermittlung erfolgt auf Honorarbasis über die vlk-Dienstleistungen GmbH. 

Gesundheitspolitische Interessenvertretung: Einbringung und Vertretung der VLK-Positionen in politische und verbandspolitische Entscheidungsprozesse auf Bundes- und Landesebene sowie aktives Mitwirken an relevanten Änderungsprozessen im Interesse der Mitglieder. Diese Leistung ist im Mitgliedsbeitrag enthalten. 

Eine Mitgliedschaft im VLK bietet somit nicht nur individuelle Unterstützung in beruflichen Belangen, sondern ermöglicht es auch, aktiv an der Gestaltung des Gesundheitswesens mitzuwirken und von einem starken Netzwerk leitender Krankenhausärztinnen und -ärzte zu profitieren.

skills: Dozentin im Fachbereich Pflege, Gesundheits-, und Sozialwissenschaften
Wissenschaftliche Leitung in forschender Tätigkeit in ESF Projekten
summary:
Als freie Dozentin im Bereich Gesundheits- und Sozialwissenschaften habe ich umfangreiche Erfahrungen in der empirischen Sozialforschung, insbesondere in qualitativer, quantitativer und Evaluationsforschung. Mein Fachwissen erstreckt sich auf Themen wie Health Care Management, Health Sciences und Public Health. Ebenso verfüge ich aufgrund langjähriger Arbeiten in Praxen und Krankenhäusern über fundierte medizinische Kenntnisse.  Meine akademischen Laufbahn habe ich mit dem Abschluss meines Doktoratsstudiums (Dr. phil. PhD) an der Exzellenz University of Gloucestershire in Großbritannien in 2018 absolviert. Ich habe zudem einen Master of Arts (MA) und einen Master of Business Administration (MBA) erlangt. 
Meine Forschungsprojekte und Publikationen decken eine breite Palette an Themen ab, darunter ESF Förderprojekte "Wandel der Arbeit im Gesundheitswesen", Digitalisierungsprojekte im Krankenhausmanagement, Versorgungsprobleme im Gesundheitswesen und die Beziehung zwischen Patientenzufriedenheit, Lebensqualität und Versorgungsqualität bei Tumorpatienten.
Darüber hinaus bin ich als doctoral supervisor an der University of Gloucestershire aktiv und begleite Promotionsprogramme im Bereich Management, Business, Sozial- und Gesundheitswesen. Meine Zusammenarbeit mit der Universität ermöglicht es mir, stets auf dem neuesten Stand der Forschung zu bleiben und innovative Ansätze in meine Lehrtätigkeit einzubringen.
Als engagierte und erfahrene Dozentin gebe ich mein Wissen und meine Erfahrungen weiter. Ich habe bereits erfolgreich Projekte geleitet und mit verschiedenen Akteuren der Gesundheitsbranche zusammengearbeitet. Meine Stärken liegen in der Entwicklung und Umsetzung von praxisnahen Lehrkonzepten sowie der Gestaltung von Weiterbildungsmaßnahmen.

headline: Professor Theater Management/ Theater Researcher at University of Music and Performing Arts Frankfurt/Main
summary:
Theater, music, literature, film, photography, the visual arts, and the humanities are my life. I was very fortunate to have grown up in a family that valued the arts - that has always shaped my life. I'm glad that I can network with such outstanding artists and scientists of all genres worldwide here on LinkedIn - it's a great privilege.
My particular passion is theater. After working as a dramaturge and dramatist, as a producer and theater director, I dedicate my life to teach and train young, talented people for careers in management, organization and planning, in dramaturgy and program planning for theaters, orchestras and festivals and independent companies. I have been teaching for over 20 years, first parallel to my work as a theater director, later as a professor. Many of our alumni are already working very successfully in the theater and music world and shaping the future of the cultural landscapes. 
My second focus is on researching the current development of the German and European, but also the American theater landscapes, from Canada to Chile. The focus is now on examining the German-speaking theater landscape in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. I am interested in uncovering crises (2016), injustice, inequality, discrimination and abuse of power (2019, 2023), dealing with the problems in cultural policy (2021/22) and the programmatic development of models for the "Theater of the Future" (2024). In recent years I have been working on a new research project called the "Ethical Theater", in which I researched the development of the theater landscape over the last 20 years and contrasted it with the future model of the Ethical Theater. The publication on this project, ETHISCHES THEATER, will appear at the end of April 2024 in German language, a translation into English is planned.

positions.description:
Chair for Artificial Intelligence and Sustainability research group.

I believe that an energy-aware perspective is imperative for developing true artificial intelligence and that an AI-first approach is imperative for solving the challenge of transitioning to a sustainable future based on renewable energy. My research is organized under two broad themes: (1) Energy in Artificial Intelligence (the use of energy in developing AI). This area encapsulates research on the tradeoffs and limitations of energy usage in solving basic AI tasks such as classification, ranking or planning & search. The notion of what constitutes AI in a machine is most famously captured by the notion of the Turing test. Currently, this is an unfair test because AI systems that offer impressive performance on tasks in restricted domains (e.g., AlphaGo) are not judged fairly: while the human brain uses around 20W-25W of energy to perform such feasts, current AI methods use orders more energy today. Energy-efficient AI methods will also be required in the years to come to reduce their energy footprint in edge and cloud computing scenarios. (2) Artificial Intelligence in Energy (the use of AI technology in generating, storing and managing energy). This area encapsulates research into the development and application of state-of-the-art AI methods to particular problems arising from the larger reliance on renewable energy, starting with more refined modeling of batteries to enable the extension of their working lifetime, all the way to the development of AI methods for control of domestic energy consumption, necessitating research into computational privacy and explainable AI.

headline: Professor at Hasso Plattner Institute
summary:
In general, I want my work to have a positive impact to many people's lives. I particularly enjoy the application of principled research to large-scale real-world problems. I enjoy learning new things every day and getting to work with (new) people. 

I fundamentally believe in a people-first approach: As a scientist, I want to solve problems that people really have - also called "working backwards" and "customer-obsession"; as a manager, I always put people (development) over project (success) - the former being "the end" and the latter being "the means" (not the other way around); as a scientific leader, I always prefer to discuss ideas with another scientist over just reading their work - learning happens faster and in a more sustained way in a dialog rather than in reading.

I do not accept existing scientific boundaries and think that the largest breakthroughs will be made at the intersection of existing disciplines. My research interests include Bayesian inference and decision making, game theory, information retrieval, natural language processing, computer vision, distributed systems, learning theory and knowledge representation and reasoning. I have published over 80 peer reviewed conference and journal papers in these fields. 

I am one of the inventors of the Drivatars™ system in the Forza Motorsport series as well as the TrueSkill™ ranking and matchmaking system in Xbox 360 Live. I also co-invented the click-prediction technology used in bing's online advertising system (adPredictor) which is used widely in the industry now. I am co-inventor for several patents relating to these inventions.

Thinking out of the box, doing stuff for the first time? I love it! As a studied Mechanical Engineer, I´ve never believed to become a Technology Strategist at one of the leading technology companies on the planet. But Digital Transformation fascinated me throughout my professional career. In the early years, I replaced drawing boards with CAD on PC´s, Paper-based lists with Databases and helped to bring a PC on every desk. After constant changes in the Tech-Industry, we´re now extending human ingenuity with Artificial Intelligence, and create a new world of Mobility in the Automotive Industry.
The passion for Automotive was one of the stable anchors in my career, and with this, I´m proud to serve Daimler globally.
In my spare time, I love to play Drums & Percussion. And also here, Change is the constant. Starting  in a Rock-Band, I play now in a Brass Orchestra together with 7 other Drummers, and in small Big Band (can something Big be small?). Playing Drumset, Mallets & Percussion is so inspiring, relaxing and pure joy. Since beginning of 2019, I play again in a Rock Band called "Charly Brown´s Parents"( https://charly-browns-parents.chayns.net/ )!
Most important is the family life. We can talk about when we met several times ;-)

Do you like to discuss how technology can change your role or business at Daimler? Get in contact with me and have a chat.

Public Health Specialist - Health Protection
positions.description:
I led disease surveillance in one of London's largest boroughs, monitoring infections, pathogens, and vaccination uptake. My responsibilities included evaluating preventive measures, launching awareness campaigns, and assessing vaccination programs. I worked closely with the UK Health Security Agency to contain disease outbreaks such as measles and tuberculosis, particularly in vulnerable areas with low vaccination rates. This cross-sectoral role involved collaboration with regional and national teams, general practitioners, pharmacies, and other stakeholders. 

Key achievements and skills:
•	Developed and implemented a community engagement strategy to identify healthcare access barriers for vulnerable and marginalized groups.
•	Led the Lambeth Council childhood vaccination program for 2023-2026, covering children aged 0-5.
•	Presented the childhood vaccination strategy to departments and the council to secure support and approval.
•	Contributed strategic insights to a new NHS health policy aimed at increasing vaccination coverage among marginalized populations.
•	Built an extensive network of relevant stakeholders to support task execution.

positions.title: Programme Lead - Vaccination Uptake
positions.description:
I led the COVID-19 vaccination programme across the region and borough, focusing on increasing vaccination uptake among vulnerable populations in Lambeth. Other areas of work included: establishing local place based leadership with priorities, developing and maintaining good relationship with primary care and reframing health challenges by exploring the needs of communities using design approaches to gain new insights into overcoming health challenges.

Key achievements and skills:
•	Managed budgets and ensured efficient resource allocation through strong project and performance management
•	Developed innovative business models to address complex public health challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic.
•	Established a grant program for advocacy organizations to address and reduce existing health and social inequalities.
•	Extensive experience in stakeholder management, effectively aligning different priorities and agendas.
•	Demonstrated adaptability and strong collaboration skills to achieve common goals and effective solutions.

positions.title: Public Health Commissioner (Children and Young People) - Childhood Obesity Lead
positions.description:
As commissioner, I aimed to ensure prevention and early intervention was addressed throughout the council and key partner organisations and led on improving the health and wellbeing of school-aged children. This included developing and commissioning services based on new and emerging evidence of best practice. I also led on the prevention of childhood obesity and commissioned services that delivered primary prevention across population, community and personal interventions.

During the Covid-19 pandemic, I led the outbreak management response to schools and early years settings across Haringey. This included strategic planning of the school testing programme of staff and students, and supporting the Covid-19 vaccination uptake programme - developing key communication materials to families within the borough. I also collected and analysed Covid-19 incidence data to inform strategic planning and reported to senior leaders within the Council on a daily/weekly basis to ensure outbreak management planning was robust.

Key achievements and skills:
•	Responded to public and government inquiries regarding services for children and youth.
•	Maintained composure in high-pressure situations.
•	Strong written and oral communication skills, including advising and information dissemination.
•	Knowledge of and experience in developing health promotion programs for children and youth.
•	Built positive relationships and received recognition for my work (nominated for Employee of the Year for handling COVID-19).

positions.title: Public Health Officer - Diet and Nutrition Lead
positions.description:
As a Public Health Officer, I developed strategies and managed public health programmes tackling public health issues around diet and nutrition for young children under 4 years and their families. This included developing, commissioning and managing services around oral health, healthy eating, environmental health, workforce training and breastfeeding to improve longitudinal outcomes for children (such as childhood obesity). 

Key achievements and skills:
•	Developed projects using service design and led stakeholder workshops to ensure project resilience.
•	Established an environmental and health strategy that engaged local food businesses to reduce the use of trans fats, salt, and sugar.
•	Implemented oral hygiene programs in childcare facilities, including training for educators and health visitors.

headline: Data Science & GenAI | Consultant | Computational Neuroscientist
summary:
I am a data science | AI researcher and consultant focusing on GenAI | LLM | NLP | RAG | Multi-Agent System (MAS) technologies. In my client and internal R&D projects, I build those systems (PoCs, demos, and in production), and give seminars and trainings about prompt engineering for ChatGPT, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and other closed- and open-source models. Starting my life as a Northern German countryside boy from a non-academic background, my journey has taken many improbable paths*. There are still many things I’d like to do, but if none of them came true, that would also be okay. 

Some of my guiding principles:
• life and the universe have no intrinsic goal – what we call purpose or meaningful are the things we value, and that's all that's needed        (to make their pursuit worthwhile and life beautiful)
• people first        (or the ultimate goal should be the flourishing of sentient beings)
• don't treat others like you wouldn't want to be treated (silver rule), treat others like you would like to be treated (golden), treat others like they would like to be treated (diamond)
• freedom, equality, and justice       (everyone should get a fair chance to flourish in their way)
• everything is transient        (and one primary cause for suffering is non-acceptance of this reality through craving and aversion)
• our selves are made up of multiple selves (recognition of this fact allows us to integrate our conflicting parts)
• judge an action by its consequences in context (don't get stuck on principles)
• done is better than perfect        (good enough is better than not done)

Making the world a better place is a noble but difficult goal. In my view, Effective Altruism (EA) is one of the better ways to care about global priority topics and the long-term future before we run out of time to find infinity.

My hobbies past and present include fine arts, photography, guitar, reading, juggling, jogging, linguistics, Ultimate Frisbee, swimming, cycling, triathlons, yoga, Lindy Hop dancing, and Vipassana meditation. 

If you are curious or inspired to connect, feel free to reach out and we can explore things together!

*Also including stints as a volunteer for people with special needs in Aberdeen, Scotland, and as a journalist in Lomé, Togo.

positions.title: Professor
positions.description: Martin is a biologist interested in studying what plastics and other snythetic agents (e.g., endocrine disrupting chemicals) do to human and ecosystem health. For that he uses state-of-the-art in vitro and in vivo bioassays to characterize the total toxicity of complex samples (e.g., leachates of plastic materials). He also applies effect-directed chemical analysis to identify novel compounds causing the observed toxicity. With this approach he aims at contributing to a more holistic understanding human and environmental exposomes. To achieve this, he is working at the interface of mechanistic toxicology, exposure science, non-target chemical analysis, and environmental health.

In India, the overall insurance penetration stands at 4.2%, 3.2 for life insurance customers, and 1% for non-life insurance customers, highlighting a substantial insurance gap. And the impact of COVID has stressed the urgency of addressing and bridging this gap more than ever.

summary:
I am an experienced leader of clinical operations teams with many years in the Life Science industry in various settings ranging from large pharma, CRO and small biotech. After a couple of years as Head of the Nordic Site Management & Monitoring team I am now Global Head of Site partnerships and engagement at AstraZeneca.

My leadership is defined by trust, clear expectations and empowerment. I have built effective and organised teams where the individual grow to increased independence and contribution to the organisation. I have experience from change management, building a growing organisation, CRO contracting and oversight management and implementing strategies and processes. I’m experienced with all aspects of clinical trials from phase I to IV in various therapeutic areas from my work in the CRO business and the more recent clinical development consultancy.

I joined the pharmaceutical business in 2003 and held positions of increasing responsibility within the CRO business, before I joined Schering-Plough in 2005 as Medical Affairs Project Manager. 

From 2006 I managed the Clinical Quality and Compliance team at Schering-Plough Sweden where I collaborated with the regional team in Europe. 

From 2008 I was Manager Clinical Operations in Sweden where I participated in several global teams. I was a member of the local clinical operations leadership team. This was during integration between Schering-Plough and MSD.

From 2011 I was Manager Clinical Operations in Sweden at the Nordic CRO NORMA A/S. I was a member of the Nordic clinical operations leadership team as head of a constantly growing team of associates.

From May 2014 I was managing the Clinical Project Management team at the drug development company SDS. This was a combined role as Director and Senior Advisor Clinical Development in a fast growing company.

From October 2018 I am heading the Nordic Site Management & Monitoring organisation at AstraZeneca, responsible for delivery of AZs clinical trials in the Nordic region.

headline: Founder and CEO at Cerebras Systems
summary:
I am a one of the founders and am CEO of Cerebras Systems. We are a team of pioneering computer architects, computer scientists, deep learning researchers, and engineers of all types. We have come together to build a new class of computer to accelerate artificial intelligence work by three orders of magnitude beyond the current state of the art. Our flagship product, the CS-3,  is the fastest AI computer in existence. It contains a collection of industry firsts, including the Cerebras Wafer Scale Engine (WSE-3). The WSE-3 is the largest chip ever built. It contains 4 trillion transistors and covers more than 46,225 square millimeters of silicon. The largest competitor's processor is only 80 billion transistors and covers 815 square millimeters. In artificial intelligence work, large chips process information more quickly producing answers in less time. As a result, neural networks that in the past took months to train, can now train in minutes and models that take tens of seconds to serve can be served immediately. 

Prior to co-founding Cerebras Systems, I was co-founder and CEO of SeaMicro.  SeaMicro (acquired by AMD for $355 million) was the pioneer in low power server technology. SeaMicro changed the trajectory of the server industry by inventing the high density, lower power, microserver category.

Prior to co-founding SeaMicro, I was Vice President of Marketing and Product Management at Force10 (acquired by Dell for $800 Million) Networks, and Vice President of Corporate Marketing and Corporate Development for Riverstone Networks (NASDAQ: RSTN) from inception through IPO. 

My passion is building teams that solve hard problems. Together we recognize large emerging opportunities, listen closely to customer requirements, build industry transforming products, and then bring these products to market in compelling fashion.

headline: Neurologist at New York Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell Medical College
summary:
Alexander E. Merkler MD, MS is board certified in neurology and the subspecialty of neurocritical care with over 10 years of experience seeing patients at New York Presbyterian Hospital/Weill Cornell in New York City. 

Dr. Merkler graduated magna cum laude from Brown University. He completed medical school at NYU School of Medicine where he was awarded the Rosenbluth grant for research. Dr. Merkler completed his Internship and neurology residency at Weill Cornell Medical Center in New York City and was nominated to be a chief resident during his final year of residency. He did a fellowship in neurocritical care at Columbia/Cornell. He has been awarded numerous prizes for clinical education and research and is currently the Cornell site director of the Columbia/Cornell neurocritical care fellowship program, the Director of the Multidisciplinary Critical Care Fellows Conference, and the Director of medical students in the Neurosciences ICU at Cornell.

Dr. Merkler is passionate about education and regularly teaches medical students, residents, and patients about complex neurological problems and disorders in easy to understand terms. He has given talks on stroke and other forms of brain and spine injury across both nationally and internationally. He also serves as a member of the American Heart Association's Young Professionals group where he routinely helps educate the public about common neurological problems such as stroke.

Dr. Merkler's research is focused primarily on stroke. He has been awarded grants from the NIH and the American Heart Association to identify novel risk factor for ischemic stroke. He has over 100 peer reviewed publications in top journals including JAMA Neurology, Neurology, and Stroke. He is an editor at the Neurohospitalist and frequently reviews articles for journals such as JAMA, JACC, and Circulation.

Led AI efforts across Salesforce, including product, applied research (frontier team), domain-specific model development, go-to-market, revenue, adoption, partnerships, acquisitions, and responsible AI. The four years I spent as a boomerang at Salesforce have been some of the most rewarding in my career.  The organization we built, execution speed, and customer and revenue impact of the generative AI platform we developed from prototype to GA product were unmatched. 

It all started in 2022 with 'Gucci GPT'-- an LLM application prototype we developed with Salesforce Research when I was leading Service Cloud, to suggest accurate, on-brand responses to customer service inquiries. We moved at startup speed and rapidly built a prototype that cut support resolution times while increasing NPS and commerce revenue. When ChatGPT captured the world's imagination that November, we were ready with our learnings and shipped 'Einstein GPT for Service and Sales' just a few months later. I was asked to take on a new role to build out an AI platform and organization to support sales, marketing, commerce, and 3p developer use cases beyond Service Cloud. 

Our team built the Einstein AI Trust Layer (prompt injection defense, toxicity filters, observability and monitoring), Prompt Builder, Model Builder (to support 3p models including Llama and OpenAI, and finetuning), Advanced RAG, and Agentforce Studio, shipping at incredible speed to get to product-market fit. We had to invent new methods to upskill our 11,000 salespeople and broader ecosystem. We started an applied research incubation team in partnership with Salesforce Research, called Frontier/Atlas, for rapid experimentation that has delivered Generative Canvas UX, LLM Benchmarks for CRM, and Atlas reasoning engine, to ensure an ongoing cadence of organic innovation. The company went through a difficult period in 2022, and these efforts helped re-energize the entire organization and ecosystem.

positions.description: Modern medicine has given us therapies for many diseases, but it's becoming consistently more challenging to develop new ones. The drug development process involves multiple steps, each of which involves a complex experiment that often fails. We believe that, for many of these phases, we can develop machine learning models to help predict the outcome of these experiments, and that those models, while inevitably imperfect, will outperform predictions based on traditional heuristics. The key will be to train powerful ML techniques on sufficient amounts of high-quality, relevant data. To achieve this goal, we are building a diverse team that spans multiple disciplines within the life science and machine learning. We bring together cutting edge methods in functional genomics and lab automation to build a bio-data factory that can produce relevant biological data at scale, allowing us to create large, high-quality datasets that enable the development of novel ML models. honors.title: Crain's 40 Under 40
honors.description:
"It would be easy to think that Gary Vaynerchuk does nothing but talk: He broke into the new-media landscape with his Wine Library YouTube channel in 2006, now hosts the #AskGaryVee channel and makes constant public appearances when not being interviewed for articles.

But the Soviet Union-born, New Jersey-bred marketing guru can also point to results, starting with WineLibrary.com, the e-commerce site he launched for his parents’ wine shop in 1996, before he even owned a computer. “I understood people were going to buy wine on the Internet,” said Mr. Vaynerchuk, who eventually increased the store’s overall sales to more than $50 million from $3 million.

Meanwhile, VaynerMedia, the social-marketing agency he founded in 2009, and which counts Pepsi and General Electric among its clients, is set to top $50 million in revenue this year."

Read more here: http://www.crainsnewyork.com/40under40/Vaynerchuk

honors.title: Fortune 40 Under 40
honors.description:
"Vaynerchuk has created two successful companies; he is a bestselling author; he can command six-figure fees for speaking engagements; and he has 1.1 million Twitter followers. But he is largely unknown to the American television-viewing public. Rather, he is Internet famous. That fame happened by design and by years of meticulous planning—and it has drawn vocal critics for a style that is loud, bombastic and blatantly self-promotional. (A sample exhortation from a video commanding people to subscribe to his YouTube channel: 'Fucking follow me, right now.')"

Read more here: http://fortune.com/2014/12/08/is-gary-vaynerchuk-vaynermedia-for-real/

honors.title: New York Times Profile
honors.description:
"Mr. Vaynerchuk is not shy about embracing the title because he is not shy about anything. A small and kinetic man with dark hair that is starting to gray, he speaks with a warm, raspy voice, as though he’s been talking all day, which he usually has. He is funny and profane and gesticulates constantly, putting air quotes around phrases that he merely wants to emphasize. Among this favorite subjects are the New York Jets, which he has vowed to buy, and his own talents, which amaze even him.

“I have as big of an ego as it gets,” he said during a recent interview, in a tone suggesting that he was simply stating the facts, “but I have, stunningly, a lot of humility considering some of the accomplishments I’ve had.”

These accomplishments include the building of VaynerMedia, which opened in 2009 and now has 290 employees, serving clients as mainstream as Del Monte, General Electric and PepsiCo. They come in the hope that Mr. Vaynerchuk can do for them what he has already done for himself: build an online audience through pluck, ubiquity and charm."

Read more here: http://www.nytimes.com/2013/11/03/technology/riding-the-hashtag-in-social-media-marketing.html?_r=1

headline: 👇 47 Page deck that will change your marketing
summary:
Gary Vaynerchuk is a serial entrepreneur and serves as the Chairman of VaynerX, the CEO of VaynerMedia, and Creator and CEO of VeeFriends, and 6x New York Times Best Selling Author. Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet. 

Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber.  

Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has ofﬁces in Amsterdam, Bangkok, Chicago, Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, New York, Tokyo, Toronto, Singapore, and Sydney. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX holding company, which also includes Eva Nosidam Productions, Gallery Media Group, The Sasha Group, VaynerSpeakers, VaynerCommerce, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League. 

Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 50 million followers and garner more than 2+ billion impressions per year across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally.  

Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, Spin Master and Pencils of Promise. He is also a longtime Well Member of charity: water.

Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets.

headline: Applied Learning Scientist
summary:
I am a learning scientist on a mission to craft the next generation of learning experiences. 

Over the past 17 years, I have worked on the design, evaluation, and improvement of a number of adaptive learning systems for learners, from 3-year-olds to professionals, for learning math, science, reading, medical science, and more.

I have also worked on assessments of 21st century competencies, curriculum design for project-based learning with VR, and learning design for a college experiential learning program. 

I think great learning experiences come about when we put the learners first, engineer for evidence, and learn as we go. And we do it together in interdisciplinary teams. 

My work is often a blend of cognitive psychology, learning analytics, efficacy research, psychometrics, and partnerships (I can't do it all myself!). You can find me translating research to learning product design and strategy, leading efficacy studies, pulling insights from learning analytics to inform product design and improvements, creating and validating assessments, establishing and maintaining partnerships with various organizations and consultants. I enjoy every aspect!

I also enjoy sharing what I've learned. Some of my recent publications:
- The Handbook of Research on Innovative Approaches to Early Childhood Development and School Readiness: https://www.igi-global.com/book/handbook-research-innovative-approaches-early/272193.

headline: Cognitive Vascular Neurologist
summary:
Dr. Hoffmann, a Professor of Neurology with the University of Central Florida, specializes in treating a wide range of neurological needs, including cognitive and behavioral neurology, stroke, migraine, neurotoxicology, traumatic brain injury, and war illness.

With 35 years of specialized neurology experience across multiple areas related to brain health, Dr. Michael Hoffmann prioritizes research-based outcomes for his patients. As a well-respected research specialist in his field, he holds two senior doctorates in cerebrovascular medicine and behavioral health, plus he has authored multiple peer-reviewed publications and four books on various neurology topics. He completed his medical degree, MBBch at the University of Witwatersrand Johannesburg, South Africa and subsequent neurology specialization and boards, FCP(SA) Neurol) administered by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of South Africa. He completed a stroke fellowship at Columbia Presbyterian Medical Center, Neurological Institute of New York, with Dr J.P, Mohr and Dr R. Sacco as mentors. 

Dr Hoffmann was promoted to full Professor in 2004 and has held academic appointments in South Africa (UKZN), Canada (Memorial University), United States (University of Kentucky, University of South Florida), courtesy appointments (University of Florida, NOVA South Eastern University) and currently with the University of Central Florida. summary: Dr. Weber is the Director Emeritus of the University of Virginia Cancer Center, and a Professor of Microbiology, Immunology and Cancer Biology at the UVA School of Medicine. His research has focused for the past 20 years on understanding cancer cell signaling, and over the past 10 years he has worked to understand how signaling can best be used as a target for cancer therapy in prostate cancer, bladder cancer, melanoma and leukemias. He has been a major contributor to the discovery and analysis of the MAP Kinase pathway, including identification of the activating phosphorylations, isolation of the first full-length clone, demonstration of a MEK activity, demonstrating that Ras could activate Raf, demonstrating that B-Raf could activate MEK, use of a phospho-specific antibody in prostate cancer patient FFPE archival samples, and showing that Ras signaling could activate the Androgen Receptor. He is among the top 1% most-cited authors in the areas of Molecular Biology & Genetics; Biology & Biochemistry (Thomson Reuters). Dr. Weber has extensive experience in basic and translational research, and in developing relationships that promote complex inter-disciplinary programs. He served as Chairman of the Scientific Advisory Board of Upstate Biotechnology, from its founding until its sale, and he serves on the External Advisory Board for several NCI-designated cancer centers..

headline: Associate Professor of Finance at University of Chicago Booth School of Business
summary:
Michael Weber joined Chicago Booth in 2014 as an Assistant Professor of Finance. His research interests include asset pricing, macroeconomics, international finance, and household finance. His work on downside risk in currency markets and other asset classes earned the 2013 AQR Insight Award and was published in the Journal of Financial Economics.

Weber is a visiting researcher at the Bureau of Labor Statistics where he studies how the inability of firms to adjust output prices to macroeconomics shocks affects their systematic risk and a member of the Macro Finance Society.

His dissertation was awarded the Top Finance Graduate Award 2014, the Best Finance PhD Award in Honor of Prof. Greenbaum 2013 (Finalist), the WFA Cubist Systematic Strategies PhD Award for Outstanding Research, the UBS Best Conference Paper Prize at the EFA Annual Meeting 2014, the 2014 EFA Best Doctoral Student Conference Paper Prize, and the Best PhD Student Paper Award, FMA European Conference 2014.

His research was covered by the Economist, Haaretz, the American Interest, Die Welt, La Stampa, among others.

Weber earned a Ph.D. and an M.S. both in Finance from the Haas School of Business at the University of California, Berkeley. Prior to his doctoral studies, he has worked in the debt advisory division of Rothschild, the Corporate Finance (M&A) advisory at KPMG, and the finance division of the Centre for European Economic Research (ZEW). He also holds a Diplom in Business Economics (with distinction) from the University of Mannheim which earned him the SEW Eurodrive dissertation award.

Weber teaches Investments at Booth. Outside of academia, he enjoys playing soccer, running, skiing, and reading.

headline: Dedicated to confronting the grand challenge of climate change.

headline: Gene Therapy | AAV Capsid Engineering |  AAV Biology |  AAV Vector Design | Gene Editing | Virologist
summary:
I’m an experienced leader in gene therapy and a specialist in molecular virology, particularly the cell biology of AAV transduction. My work is focused on efficiently delivering therapeutic DNA to the desired tissue and cell types, which is still the most formidable hurdle to harness gene therapy to help patients. This is even the case with the arguably most promising DNA delivery vehicle, recombinant AAVs. 

I’m using cutting-edge technology to isolate and design novel AAV variants that efficiently deliver their therapeutic payload to the desired tissue or cell type. For this, I draw on my extensive experience in capsid engineering and my in-depth knowledge of molecular virology and cell biology. Rigorous validation of novel AAV variants in non-human primates and human cells and organoids is critical to utilize these AAV variants in the clinic and commercialize them to help patients.

Areas of Expertise:
•   Foster a dynamic, inclusive and supportive work environment.
•   Promote collaborative efforts among teams with different skill sets to achieve company goals.
•   Ensure that the research meets the most rigorous standards.
•   Identify the most important barriers and devise strategies to overcome them.
•   Utilize my research experience in life sciences to reach company objectives and meet timelines.

Selected Career Achievements

•   As Senior Director of Viral Platforms built the capsid engineering team at Spark Therapeutics.
•   Established a combination of two AAV library-based screening approaches to isolate AAV variants that display the same tissue/cell tropism in humans and NHPs.
•  Started a selection campaign for tissue-specific AAV variants in NHPs.


•   Contributed to preclinical studies for the treatment of heart failure with AAV gene therapy. These studies resulted in a phase 1 trial and an ongoing phase 2 clinical trial.
•  Validated a promoter/enhancer combination for the exclusive expression of a therapeutic gene in the heart.
•   Established an approach to deplete anti-AAV antibodies from blood.
•   Proved that mosaic AAV capsids are useful tools to alter AAV tropism


•   As a postdoctoral fellow in the laboratory of Dr. James E. Rothman I identified the minimal machinery for membrane fusion resulting in a cover article in Cell. This article is among the top 1% cited articles and was prominently featured in Dr. Rothman’s 2013 Nobel Prize lecture.

      In its entirety, my research was published in 65 articles or book chapters.
