headline: Software Development, Project Management, Process Improvement
summary:
Life is seldom a narrow path but taking its turns as hurdles or opportunities is a measure of our mettle. 

In 2010 I graduated from Broward College and The College Academy bright eyed and ready to meet the world. My next goals were to race through my Bachelors degree proper and apply for investigative positions in the FBI or CIA hoping to find new puzzles to solve. The first half of my plan went swimmingly as I took advantage of new majors focused around the growing threat of cybercrime and its investigation. Alas while the Great Recession had began its recovery swing when I graduated in early 2014 it brought with it a rising tide of underemployed individuals chomping at the bit for their old fields of expertise. I'm sure many of you also experienced this hectic time and drought of opportunities even if you weren't a fresh faced graduate with no career experience. 

Undaunted I took a dive into the field of IT self-teaching both the Comptia Network+ and later the Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) certifications. This would land me my first job as a contractor leased to a high scoring fortune 500 company Cisco Systems, specifically a team devoted to the network management of yet another fortune 500 elite Bank of America. Practicing my newfound network talents was quite the experience but paying my dues at the help desk often resulted in long hours trying to entertain myself or fellow employees through the boredom. Eventually I found a niche aspect in our platform tools that allowed users to execute Visual Basic code to manipulate network devices. Curious I set to learning the language which set off a chain of events from revolutionizing project methodologies, to learning python, to establishing a small unofficial team with my peers, to having our little 3 man group expand to a 15+ organizationally recognized unit considered a "business critical service" to well over 100 customer accounts. 

Life is certainly full of turns but taking them in stride and being open to the experience grants you a confidence to approach tasks you wouldn't have imagined and I for one look forward to whatever the next turn in my journey is slated my way.

Simultaneously, these endeavors create a symbiotic relationship where African businesses and communities gain access to innovative technology solutions, thereby contributing to sustainable development across the continent.

Through my planned involvement in initiatives such as the International Minority Tech Roundtable and CEBOT's Tech-Africa Initiative, I hope to actively promote a vibrant ecosystem of trade, innovation, and collaboration. headline: Monetary Economics Lecturer | Future Africa Fellow & PhD Candidate: SARB Chair | Ngap Early Careers | NRF Grant | Intervarsity Convenor | Golden Key | CEBOT International Senior Fellow | Financial Services Professional
summary:
Mike is a Macroeconomist with cross-sector experience who worked as financial services sector professional & independent contractor for the past 15 years in different roles across the private & public sector: Analytics, business analyst, research, local economic development, insights, cvp design, customer experience, product design, strategy, commercialisation, credit risk & balance sheet analysis, brand, campaign management, marketing, budget management, banking regulation, sales, relationship management, skills training & instructional design, channel, complaints, operations, program & project management. 

Mike has a passion for Macroeconomics and Strategy who completed his Masters of Philosophy in Economics and Econometrics at the University of Pretoria (UP), doing 8 coursework modules and his thesis research project in 1 year, with Distinction  /cum laude grade and receiving academic honorary colors for outstanding academic performance as well as awarded an honorary student of the Golden Key International Honour Society. Mike received a Doctoral Research Fellowship position and Award from the South African Reserve Bank Chair in Monetary Economics studies, who is working towards completing his Ph.D. in Economics at UP, in collaboration with his co-supervisor at the University of Namur in Belgium. Mike has received multiple Top academic student awards during his career via a fully funded Norwegian Scholarship award for global exchange program to study Masters of Science in Economics courses abroad in Oslo, Norway and a fully funded Carnegie-Mellon award for an Economist bursary. 

Mike is an EE candidate, who was born on the Cape Flats then ended up studying at the University of Oslo, directed short film ads for CVP campaigns and worked as an Executive on Nedbank Wealth Management DivCo. Teach a child to fish! Mike started consulting in 2001 privately teaching Economics, mentoring and career coaching of Western Cape youth.

Mike is employed at Stellenbosch University as a Lecturer & Researcher for Monetary & Financial Economics, Convenor of Postgraduate Conferences, Industry Talks & Seminars, an International Senior Fellow of CEBOT (USA). His broad interests for networking themes include CVP, agile, corporate client strategy, macroeconomics & modelling, firm behaviour, econometrics, banking & wealth. 

Mike serves at his local church in multiple departments and enjoys CrossFit team competitions and Duathlon races with his wife. Mike  lives in Stellenbosch with his family, where his kids attend Rhenish Primary, actively participating in all sports.

occupation: Leading AI Products at Google

positions.title: VP of Product, ACE (AI and Compute Enablement)
positions.description:
Leading strategy and product roadmap for the AI and Compute platforms that powers all of Google products. This includes many different tools and layers of the stack, namely:

- AI Data: from human data annotation for pre and post-training to model and data lineage for GenAI data governance and RAI
- AI Model activation: tools and processes for model pre-training, fine-tuning, prompt engineering, orchestration, and model serving at scale. While we mostly focus on Gemini, we also support many other workstreams for models like Imagen, Veo, or Gemma. In fact, we also support non GenAI models internally.
- AI Frameworks: My team manages internal and external roadmap and strategy for frameworks like JAX, Keras, TensorFlow, or XLA. This also includes AI for mobile platforms now presented under the umbrella of Google AI Edge
- Compute infrastructure and efficiency: We own much of the internal AI Compute infrastructure and build efficiency tools to make sure we can bring the best out of our hardware and data centers.
- AI capacity planning and tools: Similarly, we model and plan capacity needs for all our Google needs across TPUs, GPUs, and standard compute.

Our team collaborates closely with many other teams at Google. From Google Deepmind on the research side, all the way to Google Cloud and our many product teams (Search, Ads, Youtube...)

headline: Leading AI Products at Google
summary:
Leading the ACE (AI and Compute Enablement) product team at Google, building AI product solutions that serve all of Google's products, including Google Cloud.

I am a technical/product leader with over two decades of experience in leading and developing cutting-edge AI and ML solutions for various domains, such as e-commerce, health, media, and education. My passion is to create innovative products that leverage the power of data and algorithms to solve real-world problems and improve people's lives.

Besides starting my own company, Curai Health, using state-of-the-art AI to provide the best possible care to everyone, I have led teams in companies such as LinkedIn and Quora. I am probably best known as having started and led the team that built the famous Netflix Recommendations.

I have a PhD and deep technical background in Machine Learning and AI, and I have published over 100 papers in top-tier conferences and journals, and hold several patents in AI and ML. I have also advises and mentored startups to scale their AI capabilities and strategies.
